- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.20 over 3 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price action (last 7–10 days); adjust downward by 0.5–2% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misjudges mean reversion; use 14-day EMA as anchor for correction.
